text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The SWA Mineworkers Union (SWAMU) reacts to a report from the Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN) in which MUN general-secretary Peter Naholo accused SWAMU of attempting to split workers into a white and black camp.

- The programme of late registration of births has had to be extended for the second time. Now every Namibian is expected to carry a birth certificate by May 31. The ministry of home affairs says after that deadline it will not be able to grant a further extension for financial reasons.

- Union dissatisfaction may result in disunity within the ruling party SWAPO. The Namibia Public Workers Union (NAPWU) is openly opposing the government's plans for commercialisation of government departments.

- Twenty five thousand cases of Malaria, among them 14 deaths have been recorded in the Kavango and Caprivi regions between December 1996 and March 1997. The Ministry of Health has sent more medical personnel and medicines to the areas to cope wit the increase in malaria cases.
